code_base.note: no renderer, gameplay, test or asset file differs from main, so every line reference in this inventory is valid for a reader of main

scope: Every 3D model the renderer can draw from data, plus every renderer dispatch path that can supply geometry and every visual element that is not a discrete model replacement. Environment props are included in the row set but carry status 'unknown_needs_owner_scope_decision': they are inventoried so the migration cannot silently omit them, not because they are in scope.

does_not_cover: any other hull, station, satellite or installation
catalogue-wide rollout or a production default switch

owner_scope_decisions.decided_by: owner (Lukasz Jawor), in chat; raw wording preserved below

binds_to.note: Binds the scope questions asked in that matrix. It is a scope and plan approval, not an approval of any model design, and not authorization to merge, activate the trio or change the production default.

answers.question: Are planet bodies (procedural equirect-textured spheres) permanently out of the model catalogue, or in scope?
answers.answer: in scope — bring into the catalogue
answers.raw_owner_wording: 1.) scope exceptions: let bring them into catalog.

answers.question: Asteroid/neutral environment props are per-instance procedural; keep procedural or replace with a shared authored prop?
answers.answer: in scope — bring into the catalogue

answers.question: Does the menu 3D backdrop stay a baked movie, or is it in the catalogue?
answers.answer: in scope — bring into the catalogue
answers.open_sub_question: Whether the menu scene is then drawn live or stays baked per catalogue revision is an S02/S04 implementation choice, not part of this scope answer. The baked path exists to avoid paying battle-scene cost behind every menu, so the bake-per-revision reading is recorded as the default unless the owner prefers a live menu.

answers.question: syndicate:bomber, syndicate:battleship, syndicate:supercapital are declared in SHIP_KEYS but no data row selects them. Keep or remove?
answers.raw_owner_wording: 2.) plan the hulls . Battleshipo and capitol shoudl be buidl in ship yard, bomber in fighter yard.

answers.question: Which batch order?
answers.answer: as recommended: B1 Alliance combat hulls, then B2 squadrons/logistics, B3 stations, B4 satellites and planet installations, B5 environment props

answers.question: Approve the batch plan?
answers.answer: approved — as a plan and as scope. This does not approve any model design, and S06 still requires per-asset owner approval with an enumerated list.

consequences: Environment props move from 'scope decision required' to in-scope work. The planet kinds (E05) and the asteroid field (E07) become authoring targets in batch B5.
The menu backdrop (E23) gets its own inventory row so the decision is bound to a binding rather than to a sentence: menu:cinematic:backdrop.
The three unreachable SHIP_KEYS stay in the registry as planned hulls with a recorded production site.
The starfield sky dome, star, nebula and jump point were proposed keep-procedural and were not among the questions asked; they are carried as proposed, not as owner-approved.

planned_hulls.owner_rule: Battleships and capital ships build at the shipyard; bombers build at the fighter platform (the owner's 'fighter yard').

grounding.mechanism: game/systems/construction.py decides buildability from the station's builds_ships list: an exact ship id, or ['*'] for any ship
grounding.shipyard.builds_ships: ['*'] — already accepts every ship, so battleship/capital production at the shipyard holds today
grounding.fighter_platform_consequence: This list is explicit, so a new bomber hull is unbuildable until its data id is added to it. That is a data change S06 must make alongside the hull, not a model change.

hulls.note: the syndicate currently fields only raid_squadron, which resolves to syndicate:fighter; there is no syndicate bomber data row

campaign_coverage.conclusion: every ship and station the campaign references resolves to an inventoried binding
